questions.q: What does cloud computing actually mean, beyond "someone else's computer"?
options: Renting compute, storage, and networking from a provider — available in minutes, billed by actual usage, resizable without buying anything new
Running software only on a local personal computer
A marketing term with no real technical definition
Physically shipping a server to a customer's office
questions.explain: The joke undersells the real shift: on-demand availability, usage-based billing, and resizing without a hardware purchase.

questions.q: What is the real difference between CapEx and OpEx?
options: CapEx is a large upfront purchase that depreciates over years; OpEx is an ongoing cost that scales with actual use
CapEx and OpEx are two names for exactly the same kind of spending
OpEx only applies to physical hardware purchases
CapEx is always cheaper than OpEx in every situation
questions.explain: Cloud computing shifts most infrastructure spending from CapEx into OpEx, which is why a startup can run production infrastructure without raising capital for hardware first.

questions.q: Which of these is one of the five real characteristics that define cloud computing?
options: Rapid elasticity — scaling resources up or down to match real demand
Requiring a hardware purchase order before any resource can be provisioned
A fixed monthly fee regardless of actual usage
Access restricted only to an internal, on-premises network
questions.explain: The five characteristics are on-demand self-service, broad network access, resource pooling, rapid elasticity, and measured service.

questions.q: What does "measured service" mean as one of the five cloud characteristics?
options: Billing is based on actual consumption, like compute-hours or gigabytes stored, not a flat fee
Every cloud provider charges exactly the same price
Usage must be manually reported to the provider each month
Resources can never be measured or monitored at all
questions.explain: Measured service is what makes usage-based, OpEx-style billing possible in the first place.

Nothing — it's meant to be taken last, as a capstone review
Only non-Microsoft cloud provider courses
